theme: Graphite GPU backend and new APIs
highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.151.0 dev adds the Graphite GPU backend, async ReadPixels, and a new Vulkan.Silk.NET integration package.
highlights_body: The new Graphite rendering engine (Vulkan, Metal, Dawn) is now bindable via SkiaSharp. A backend-neutral async RequestReadPixels API covers both Ganesh and Graphite surfaces. Nano Server gains FreeType font support, and SKData.SaveTo avoids a double buffer copy.

bullets.detail: Multiple rounds of upstream chrome/m151 bug-fix merges were applied to the Skia submodule, keeping the bundled engine current with Google's stable branch.
New bindings expose the Skia Graphite rendering engine for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn backends, providing an alternative to the Ganesh path for hardware-accelerated rendering.
SKImage and SKSurface gain RequestReadPixels, an async API that works across both Ganesh and Graphite GPU backends for reading pixel data back from GPU surfaces.
A new NuGet package bridges SkiaSharp's Vulkan surface types with Silk.NET's Vulkan bindings, making it straightforward to integrate SkiaSharp into Silk.NET-based applications.

bullets.lead: Binding generation is now deterministic across platforms
bullets.detail: The C# binding generator produces byte-for-byte identical output regardless of which OS runs it, eliminating spurious diffs in generated files when contributors work on different platforms.

bullets.lead: CoTaskMem pixel-buffer leak in SKImage.Create failure path
bullets.detail: When SKImage.Create raster failed (e.g. invalid info), the CoTaskMem-allocated pixel buffer was not freed. The buffer is now correctly released on all error paths.
The SaveTo path previously copied data into a managed byte array and then wrote it; it now writes directly from the native buffer, halving memory traffic for large blobs.
GetEncodedText no longer allocates an intermediate string on the null-terminated fast path. SKRuntimeEffectUniforms pre-sizes its uniform lookup map to the known count, eliminating rehashing.

bullets.lead: FreeType font support on Windows Nano Server
bullets.detail: SkiaSharp now uses FreeType for font rendering on Nano Server, where no system font stack is available, unblocking text output in containerized Windows workloads.

bullets.lead: Containerized test coverage: Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, Nano Server
bullets.detail: CI now validates SkiaSharp on Azure Linux, Alpine Linux (musl libc), and Windows Nano Server containers, extending the verified platform matrix.

bullets.lead: Windows native builds: MSVC environment initialized once per build
bullets.detail: The MSVC toolchain environment is now set up once at the start of each native build rather than per-target, fixing intermittent failures and reducing build time.

contributor_summaries.jeffska: FreeType font support on Windows Nano Server, fixing text rendering in containerized Windows workloads.
contributor_summaries.mmitche: Windows native build fix: MSVC environment initialization consolidated to once per build.
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn.
